preamble: In a number of Chinese dialects the aspirated initial *tʰ (Middle Chinese 透; Proto-Min *th in Min) lost its stop closure and became a dorsal fricative. Chang Kun (1994) surveys the change: in most affected dialects (e.g. Nanchang Gan, the Pearl River Delta Yue dialects) the result is glottal h, but in Shao–Jiang Min Guangze in northwestern Fujian it is velar x throughout, and in Wenchang Hainanese the reflex of Proto-Min *th is x, kept apart from the 曉 initial, which is read h.

examples.note: Proto-Min *th is kept as tʰ in Xiamen, Fuzhou, Jian'ou and Shaowu.
透 initial read x; 曉 words such as 毀 'destroy' have h (hui).
Chang's comparative table transcribes the same Wenchang words with h.

sources: Chang, K. 張琨 (1994). The Changes of *th>h/x and *tsh>th among Chinese Dialects 漢語方言中的*th>h/x和*tsh>th. Bulletin of the Institute of History and Philology, Academia Sinica 65(1): 19-36. https://www1.ihp.sinica.edu.tw/en/Publications/Bulletin/121/Article/498
